In mathematics,  '''Arf semigroups''' are certain subsets of the non-negative [[integer]]s closed under [[addition]], that were studied by {{harvs|txt|last=Arf|first=Cahit|authorlink=Cahit Arf|year= 1948}}. They appeared as the semigroups of values of [[Arf ring]]s. 

A subset of the integers forms a [[monoid]] if it includes zero, and if every two elements in the subset have a sum that also belongs to the subset. In this case, it is called a "numerical semigroup".
A numerical semigroup is called an Arf semigroup if, for every three elements ''x'', ''y'', and ''z'' with ''z'' = min(''x'', ''y'', and ''z''), the semigroup also contains the element {{nowrap|''x'' + ''y'' &minus; ''z''}}.

For instance, the set containing zero and all even numbers greater than 10 is an Arf semigroup.
